newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares end higher, size up resistance.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares end higher, size up resistance.

text.p: Austrian shares advanced in slim volume on Monday, buoyed by demand for a handful of ATX shares and selected second line stocks.
The blue-chip ATX index closed 14.66 points, or 1.13 percent, higher at 1,309.70 -- just short of the intra-day high of 1,309.84. Overall 18 gainers outweighed three decliners.
Traders said ATX buying interest centred on oil and chemicals concern OMV, engineering group VA Tech and Vienna airport company Flughafen Wien.
They saw added support from a firm dollar. "Unlike Germany, the Austrian market had not fully factored in the dollar's strength," said one dealer.
He forecast caution would reign on Tuesday, however, ahead of the FOMC meeting in the United States. After that the ATX index would need to vault resistance at 1,310 to 1,312 points.
"That will be the moment of truth," he said.
A second trader expected the market to continue on an upward path until mid-week but warned a downward correction lay ahead unless volume picked up.
July ATX futures stood 8.2 points up at 1,307.
Luxury stocking maker Wolford was the biggest gainer among ATX shares. It firmed 52 schillings, or 4.57 percent, to 1,190 schillings on 61,491 lots.
Wolford was closely followed by carton board maker Mayr-Melnhof, up 27 schillings, or 4.56 percent, to 630 schillings on 33,747 lots.
"The strength of these two stocks says more about the market's illiquidity," said a trader.
Regional utility EVN was the biggest decliner, down 27 schillings, or 1.68 percent, at 1,580 schillings.
The broad-based Vienna bourse index rose 3.86 points to 477.71. -- Vienna newsroom, +43-1 531 12 254
